newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 96 deficit/GDP 4.2 pct, govt says no problem.
newsitem.headline: French 96 deficit/GDP 4.2 pct, govt says no problem.

text.p: France's national statistics office INSEE said on Tuesday the public deficit as a proportion of gross domestic product (GDP) came in at 4.2 percent in 1996.

This was a touch above the government's official forecast of 4.1 percent. The government has vowed to cut its public deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997, the strict level required to qualify for European monetary union.
A senior finance ministry official told Reuters that the figure had been changed by "rounding up".
"It was a big 4.1, now it's a small 4.2," the official said. "It's a question of a few billion (francs). It changes nothing."
INSEE said the 1996 figure followed a 1995 deficit figure of five percent of GDP.
